title: Does an Executable Emulator Validator Reduce Semantic Failures in LLM-Generated Network Configuration Changes?
abstract: We report a fully preregistered paired experiment (CNSM2026-A-prereg-v1) that tested whether inserting an executable emulator validator into a generate→validate→repair pipeline reduces semantic/network-level failures versus an LLM-only suggestion workflow. Using a deterministic paired design with N=120 intent→configuration tasks (40 per topology class: edge, core, leaf–spine) we produced one shared initial candidate per task via gpt-5-mini (model_calls_used = 120) and evaluated the identical candidate under both conditions. The guarded pipeline used deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (version 5.0) with at most one repair iteration per guarded episode. Observed outcomes: baseline successes = 120/120; guarded successes = 120/120; paired contingency: n_11=120, n_10=0, n_01=0, n_00=0. Exact two-sided McNemar p = 1.0; paired-difference estimate = 0.00; paired-bootstrap-percentile 95% CI = [0.00, 0.00] (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). Validator traces record repair_applied = false for every guarded episode. We expand methodological detail, representative diagnostics grounded in archived validator traces and task manifests, reproducibility guidance tied to the preregistered artifacts, and discuss construct/external validity limits and design recommendations for future confirmatory studies.

sections.introduction: LLM-based systems that translate operator intent into device configuration promise productivity gains for network operations, but syntactically plausible command sequences can violate temporal and stateful workflow invariants (for example, changing MTU without an enforced shutdown or performing an unsafe uplink switchover) and thereby produce semantic failures visible only in closed-loop execution. Prior work argues for integrating deterministic verification, emulation, or veto layers so generated candidates are validated before enactment. Measuring the marginal contribution of such validators requires experimental designs that expose stateful and order-dependent invariants rather than token- or syntax-level correctness alone. We conducted a preregistered paired confirmatory experiment (CNSM2026-A-prereg-v1) whose mechanistic question was whether an executable network emulator validator plus a bounded repair policy reduces emulator-observed semantic failures relative to an LLM-only suggestion workflow when the identical generator output is scored by both pipelines. The paired shared-generation design removes generator sampling variance so any observed discordance can be attributed to the validator/repair subsystem. The run produced a ceiling outcome (every shared candidate satisfied the emulator checks). This paper reports the exact execution and analysis results, explains why the ceiling occurred in light of the design choices, and draws methodological lessons for future confirmatory evaluations.
sections.related_work: Executable, emulation-grounded benchmarks and tool papers have repeatedly shown that syntax-level metrics miss closed-loop failure classes—make-before-break violations, availability-group breaches, and order-dependent invariants—and that deterministic verification layers can reduce enacted semantic errors when generators err. Recent benchmark and tool efforts (NetConfArena; Benchmarking LLM-Driven Network Configuration Repair; Aether; NetConf-like executable testbeds) demonstrate the utility of closed-loop tests that apply generated commands to an emulator or digital twin and check end-to-end invariants. Surveys and architecture papers on agentic NetOps document that guarded architectures (veto layers, canaries, generate→validate→repair) are recurring proposals for operational safety. These prior studies also emphasize two evaluation pitfalls we addressed: (1) generating distinct candidates per condition conflates generator variance with verification efficacy, and (2) paired shared-generation designs isolate verification marginal effects but can produce ceiling outcomes when the generator/prompt is well matched to the task bank. Our work complements that literature by reporting a fully preregistered, artifact-backed paired test and by archiving fine-grained validator traces that permit a mechanistic diagnosis of a degenerate confirmatory outcome.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and primary estimand. The experiment was preregistered (CNSM2026-A-prereg-v1). The design is paired-binary with N=120 distinct intent→configuration tasks deterministically partitioned into three topology classes (edge/core/leaf–spine; 40 each). The primary estimand is the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline; the prespecified confirmatory test is the exact two-sided McNemar test and a paired-bootstrap-percentile 95% CI with 10,000 resamples and seed = 1729. The preregistration fixed exclusion rules, a repair budget (≤1 repair per guarded episode), contamination controls, deterministic reset semantics, and a sensitivity-analysis plan.

Task generation, constraints, and validator semantics. Tasks were produced by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5; each task payload encoded initial_state, expected_final_state, a natural-language intent, an explicit required_sequence (canonical ordered operations), and difficulty metadata (changed_interface_count, dependency_rule_count, required_command_count, level). Workflow_policies such as must_be_down_for_fields, final_group_constraints, and make-before-break patterns were expressed in the task payload and enforced by the validator as executable checks. The guarded pipeline used deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator_version = 5.0). For each guarded episode the validator (a) applied the shared candidate in an emulator seeded from the task initial_state, (b) enforced workflow_policies, and (c) emitted a structured validator_trace containing validation_before, validation_after, parsed_command_count, required_command_count, violation_count, violation_codes, observed_touched_field_count, and repair_applied. The repair policy permitted at most one repair iteration when violation_count>0.

Shared-generation paired design and instrumentation. For each pair we issued one shared generation call to gpt-5-mini and reused that identical candidate for baseline and guarded scoring. Model-level accounting: model_calls_used = 120; cache_miss_count = 120; cache_hit_count = 0. The harness enforced deterministic emulator resets between tasks, container checksum verification, and contamination checks (duplicate-output detection and cross-condition cache-key reuse detection); none were triggered. Deterministic reconciliation recorded planned_episode_count = 240; completed_episode_count = 240; failed_episode_count = 0; complete_pair_count = 120.

Scoring rule, outcome definition, and planned inference. Each paired observation produced a binary semantic outcome (pass when the emulator-observed final_state satisfied the task's expected_final_state and the required_sequence under scoring_rule = full_intent_constraint_validation; fail otherwise). The preregistered analysis used exact McNemar (two-sided) and the paired-bootstrap-percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). The preregistered power calculation assumed baseline failure ≈ 0.40 and targeted an absolute reduction of 0.15; we report that assumption and demonstrate how the observed baseline invalidates that planned power justification. All instrumentation logs, validator traces, and scoring artifacts were archived for auditability.
sections.results:
Execution and confirmatory outcome. The run completed without technical exclusions. Condition summaries: baseline successes = 120, baseline failures = 0; guarded successes = 120, guarded failures = 0. The paired contingency table was n_11 = 120, n_10 = 0, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 0. Exact two-sided McNemar p-value = 1.0; paired-difference estimate = 0.00. The paired-bootstrap-percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.00, 0.00]. Validator traces record repair_applied = false for every guarded episode, so no repair-provider-call artifacts were produced.

Representative per-task diagnostics (artifact-grounded). Representative task manifests and validator traces illustrate why every pair passed. Example artifacts archived for inspection include: task-000001 (pattern shutdown_configure_restore): parsed_command_count = 4, required_command_count = 4, observed_touched_field_count = 3, validation_after.valid = true, violation_count = 0; task-000002 (pattern make_before_break_uplink_switchover): parsed_command_count = 2, required_command_count = 2, observed_touched_field_count = 2, validation_after.valid = true, violation_count = 0; task-000003 (pattern paired_link_atomic_mtu_change): parsed_command_count = 6, required_command_count = 6, observed_touched_field_count = 4, validation_after.valid = true, violation_count = 0. These per-episode traces show the shared_initial_candidate matched the encoded required_sequence sufficiently for the validator to deem the configuration valid under the harness's executable checks.

Subgroup summaries and accounting. Success was uniform across topology classes (Edge: 40/40; Core: 40/40; Leaf–spine: 40/40). Deterministic reconciliation and provider-call audit: planned_episode_count = 240; completed_episode_count = 240; failed_episode_count = 0; complete_pair_count = 120; hosted_model_call_event_count = 120; cache_miss_count = 120; cache_hit_count = 0; all deterministic consistency checks passed.

Statistical interpretation. The McNemar test returns p = 1.0 because there are zero discordant pairs (n_10 = n_01 = 0). The bootstrap CI is degenerate at [0.00, 0.00] under the prespecified resampling because every resample reproduces the same paired contingency when no discordant pairs exist. The preregistered power calculation assumed baseline failure ≈ 0.40; the observed baseline = 0.00 invalidates that assumption and renders the originally targeted effect-size power calculation inapplicable for this execution.
sections.discussion:
Meaning of a ceiling outcome. The paired shared-generation design isolates the marginal contribution of the validator/repair subsystem by removing generator variance across conditions. For this task corpus and the declared model/prompt the shared generator outputs satisfied the emulator-enforced workflow_policies in every tested instance, so the guard observed zero violations and did not apply repairs. That ceiling is an informative scientific outcome: it documents that, under the specific combination of a deterministic synthetic task bank, deterministic task generator (deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5), a frozen prompt and gpt-5-mini, the generator produced valid candidates such that an executable validator had no corrective work to perform.

Mechanistic diagnosis and implications. Artifact-grounded validator_traces reveal that parsed_command_count matched required_command_count for representative tasks and that validation_before.valid and validation_after.valid were true. This indicates alignment between the generator's output format/ordering and the harness's required_sequence encodings. The operational implication is twofold: (1) when generators are well calibrated to a curated task set, guards may be idle but still provide audit value through structured traces (violation_codes empty, repair_applied=false); (2) demonstrating repair utility empirically requires a design that introduces generator variance or harder/less-aligned tasks so violations occur with non-negligible frequency.

Design trade-offs and concrete recommendations. The experiment makes explicit a trade-off between internal validity and the ability to exercise repair behavior. Prespecified, artifact-grounded recommendations (each anticipated in the preregistration) include: (a) allow independent generation per condition so validators can intercept generator sampling errors at the cost of modeling generator variance in analysis; (b) include prespecified prompt perturbations or adversarial variants on a subset of tasks to raise generator-induced violation incidence while retaining paired blocks for internal control; (c) stratify tasks toward higher dependency_rule_count or required_command_count to increase difficulty; and (d) include exploratory arms with expanded repair budgets (>1 iteration) to study repair convergence and provider-call costs when repairs are applied. Implementing these variants within the same harness and artifact schema would exercise validator/repair behavior while preserving auditability.

Auditability and reproducibility benefits of executable validators. Even when unused, deterministic validators that emit structured traces (checked rules, touched fields, violation_codes, repair_applied flags) materially improve post-hoc auditability and mechanistic diagnosis. The archived reconciliation summary (complete_pair_count = 120; planned_episode_count = 240; completed_episode_count = 240; failed_episode_count = 0) and provider-call audits (hosted_model_call_event_count = 120; cache_miss_count = 120; cache_hit_count = 0) provide transparent accounting of model usage and execution stage counts. These artifacts permit targeted follow-up experiments that relax shared-generation constraints or vary generator families while preserving the same executable tests.

Threats to validity. Internal validity for this run is high (deterministic provisioning, deterministic reconciliation, no technical exclusions). Construct validity is limited because workflow_policies and task payloads are synthetic encodings that may underrepresent vendor heterogeneity, partial telemetry observability, and noisy real-world incidents; some production failure modes may therefore be absent. External validity is constrained by the synthetic deterministic task corpus, a single hosted model (gpt-5-mini), and a frozen prompting strategy. Conclusion validity is affected by the statistical ceiling: the preregistered power calculation assumed baseline failure ≈ 0.40; the observed baseline = 0.00 violates that assumption and makes the McNemar confirmatory test uninformative for the originally targeted effect size. These limitations are documented in the preregistration and archived artifacts.

Practical takeaway. The principal operational lesson is that experimental choices (shared-generation paired design, curated synthetic tasks, frozen prompt) determine whether repair policies can be empirically exercised. When the generator is well matched to the task bank, an executable validator may be idle but still provides audit-grade traces. To quantify practical repair utility under realistic generator variance, future confirmatory studies should combine independent-condition generation, controlled prompt perturbations, and higher-complexity tasks while preserving the same executable validation semantics.
sections.conclusion: In a fully preregistered paired experiment (N=120) comparing an executable generate→validate→repair pipeline against an LLM-only workflow under a deterministic harness with gpt-5-mini, every shared initial candidate satisfied the emulator's required_sequence and workflow_policies. The experiment produced n_11 = 120, a paired-difference estimate of 0.00 (exact McNemar p = 1.0; paired-bootstrap 95% CI = [0.00, 0.00], 10,000 resamples, seed = 1729), and validator.repair_applied = false in all guarded episodes. Scientifically, the result documents a ceiling for this curated synthetic task bank and illustrates how a shared-generation paired design isolates validator/repair effects but can mask repair benefits when the generator is well calibrated for the chosen corpus. Methodologically, preregistered, artifact-rich paired designs combined with executable validators that emit fine-grained traces permit reproducible diagnosis of degenerate confirmatory outcomes and support principled follow-up designs to quantify repair utility under realistic generator variance.

limitations: Confirmatory scope: results are narrowly scoped to the preregistered synthetic task set, a single hosted model (gpt-5-mini), and a frozen prompting strategy; generalization to production heterogeneity is limited.
Synthetic task provenance: tasks were synthetic/deterministic and may underrepresent noisy, adversarial, or multi-vendor production incidents; external validity to live networks is constrained.

Shared-generation design: using a single shared initial generation per paired task isolates validator/repair efficacy but precludes detection of generation-variance effects; this choice contributed to the ceiling outcome and limits inference about repair utility on independently generated invalid outputs.

Validator fidelity: the deterministic emulator/validator is reproducible but simplifies heterogeneity present in multi-vendor, partially observable production environments; some real-world failure modes may not be exposed.

Statistical ceiling: baseline success reached 100% on the tested task bank, violating the preregistered power assumptions (targeted absolute reduction = 0.15) and rendering the McNemar confirmatory test uninformative for demonstrating the preregistered effect size.
